script: That sudden red, fleshy bulge in the corner of your dog's eye has a real name, vets call it cherry eye. Dogs actually have a third eyelid most people never notice, tucked into the inner corner of the eye, and it holds a small tear-producing gland. In some dogs, especially certain breeds, the tissue holding that gland in place is weaker than normal, and the gland can pop out of position, showing up as that round red lump. It looks alarming, but it's not usually painful in the early stages, just uncomfortable and irritating for your dog. It also won't fix itself by going back into place on its own, so it's one of those things that genuinely needs a vet visit rather than a wait-and-see approach, since that gland plays a real role in keeping the eye properly lubricated long term. Catching it early and getting it treated quickly almost always leads to a simple, straightforward fix. So if you ever spot that red bump, it's not something to panic about, but it is something to actually act on. Want more real dog behavior insight? The link's below.
